standards: Identify, from a short client brief, who will read the letter and what that reader needs to know, and state the letter's purpose first in one sentence.
Rewrite a sample letter in plain words, replacing legal jargon with everyday terms that keep the meaning, and fit it onto one page.
Apply a simple readability test to a drafted letter, then ask a colleague to read it, and adjust any hard sentences the test or reader finds.
Add to a letter the next step and its date, and check that every date and figure matches the source documents given.
Draft a full client letter from a case card, with purpose first, then facts, then next step and date, in plain words and under one page.
Pass the check by editing a sample letter against the checklist so it is plain, accurate, under one page and ends with the next step and date.
Name the main parts of a sample contract and find each numbered clause in order, so that no clause in the eight-clause sample is skipped.
Summarize each clause of a sample contract in one sentence, so the summary confirms that you have understood what the clause says.
Identify the risk clauses in a sample contract, such as payment terms, termination, liability, indemnity and change of terms, listing at least five with a question each.
Give each flagged clause a high, medium or low risk rating with a stated reason, and put the clauses in order of priority.
Propose safer wording for a risky clause, such as a stated cap or a notice period, and record agree, query or escalate against the checklist.
Pass the assessment by completing the clause table for a new sample contract so a supervisor can follow every summary, rating, reason and suggestion.
Arrange the papers in a messy sample file into the standard order: index, instructions, correspondence, dated notes, documents, billing and closing checklist.
Record each decision in a scenario at the time it is made, with who, what, when and why, and date every note.
Close a file by completing every item on the closing checklist: the outcome, the documents returned and the retention date.
State who may see a file and how long it is kept under a given policy, and name how to dispose of records safely afterwards.
Reorder a file with loose notes and no time record, fill the gaps with an index, dates and version, and complete its checklist.
Pass the check by showing a sample file in standard order with dated decisions, a completed closing checklist and the correct retention period.
State a testable question and a hypothesis for a given topic, such as paint drying time, with one measure that can be answered with a number.
Choose a control group and a measure with units for a question, and keep all conditions the same except the one thing changed.
Decide how many repeats are needed for each group, and explain that repeats show the natural spread in the results.
Write a method with materials, steps, measures and units that is clear enough for another person to repeat exactly.
Check a partner's method against the checklist, find unclear steps and at least four sources of error, and suggest a fix for each.
Pass the assessment by writing a repeatable method for a new question, with a control, a measure, repeats and listed sources of error.
Calculate the mean and the spread of a small data set with correct arithmetic and units, as in groups of three plant heights.
Plot group means from the numbers given, labelling each axis with a name and a unit so the plot can be read alone.
Add error bars of one standard deviation to a plot and state in the caption what the bars show.
Judge from two plots whether a difference is larger than the spread, and say that a gap alone does not prove a cause.
Write a one-paragraph result for a figure that states the difference and spread and does not claim more than the data show.
Pass the assessment by calculating, plotting and interpreting two small data sets, then writing a paragraph that stays within what the data show.
Arrange a result table into a short report with the standard sections: title, abstract, introduction, methods, results, discussion, limits and references.
Cite every source in a report using one agreed style, kept the same throughout, so each claim can be traced.
Write at least three honest sentences on limits, covering what was not tested and the possible errors, for a small one-site study.
Edit a draft paragraph into clear, short sentences with plain words and no claim beyond the data.
Write a full short report from a result table, with all sections in place, results kept apart from discussion, and a limits paragraph.
Pass the check by producing a short report in the standard order with one citation style, honest limits and no claims beyond the data.
Explain why a client history is taken before treatment, naming how it protects the client from harm and why it is recorded.
Ask the required history questions in order, covering allergies, skin conditions, medicines, pregnancy and previous reactions, so every required field is complete.
Record a client's answers clearly on the form, dated and signed, and note any refusal to answer, while keeping the form secure.
Identify from sample histories the reasons not to proceed and refer the client on to the right person, with at least 7 of 8 correct.
Role-play taking a history from a client who mentions recent surgery or a skin condition, asking follow-up questions and deciding on referral.
Pass the check by completing a history form for a case card and deciding correctly whether to proceed or refer on.
Explain why infection control matters in a treatment room and list the risks to clients and staff when a step is missed.
Demonstrate hand cleaning with every step in order, before and after each client and after removing gloves, against a checklist.
Choose the cleaning level for each of six items, such as towel, tweezers and gloves, and keep clean and used items apart.
Record cleaning on the log with date, item, method and initials, so there is proof of the routine for a lead to check.
Demonstrate the full routine on a live case where a reusable tool touched skin, choosing the cleaning level and completing the log.
Pass the check by showing hand cleaning, tool cleaning levels and a complete log, following the local rule and product instructions.
Explain what consent means, including that it must be understood and that a client can withdraw it at any time.
Explain a treatment to a client in plain words, covering benefits, risks, aftercare and what the client can refuse.
Complete the standard consent form with the date, the client's name and what was agreed, and keep it securely in the client file.
Review a signed form when anything changes, explain the change, and record the new agreement before going ahead.
Role-play obtaining consent from a client who hesitates, checking understanding before the signature and recording it on the template.
Pass the check by explaining a treatment in plain words, completing the form correctly, and finding any missing item in a sample form.
